key_insight: A computational search identified 58 candidate CuI-based ternary p-type transparent conductors and generalized design rules beyond oxide materials.
engineering_relevance: These candidates could expand transparent hole-conducting material options for electronics and tandem photovoltaics, pending experimental validation.
method: Search X–Cu–I structures using minima hopping and density functional theory.
Filter for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Analyze Cu coordination and electronic structure to generalize valence-band design rules.
evidence_signal: Of 58 candidates, 49 were previously unreported and 20 were predicted p-type degenerate semiconductors; Cu₂FI₂ had a calculated 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m₀ hole effective mass.
watch_item: Computational screening does not establish experimental synthesizability, measured conductivity, or performance in photovoltaic devices.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
